claims.text: The initial sub-10 nm equiatomic Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles are disordered single-phase solid solutions.
The sluggish-diffusion assumption breaks down above 700 K in sub-10 nm Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.
Surface-energy-driven segregation and Ostwald ripening dominate the structural evolution of these nanoparticles.
Rapid atomic exchange at high-curvature surfaces overrides bulk thermodynamic stabilization.
Au-Cu and Ni-Cu have negative enthalpies of mixing under the relevant conditions.
Negative mixing enthalpies of specific binary pairs favor local segregation despite configurational entropy.
The high surface energy of sub-10 nm particles lowers the activation barrier for surface diffusion.
Au and Cu rapidly segregate to the nanoparticle surface because they have relatively low surface energies.
Ostwald ripening causes the dissolution and selective loss of the smallest particles.
Particle faceting occurs to minimize total surface energy.
Particles smaller than 5 nm will be lost during heating.
The surviving particles will grow and develop faceted, compositionally segregated morphologies.
Au-rich shells or cores may form rather than a stable single-phase solid solution.
High mixing entropy and lattice distortion are commonly invoked as characteristic HEA phenomena associated with sluggish diffusion.
HEA theory predicts that the target nanoparticles remain spherical, equiatomic, single phase, and stable up to 1000 K.
Surface effects dominate specifically below 10 nm, whereas sluggish diffusion may remain operative above 50 nm or in bulk material.
Sluggish diffusion in bulk HEAs is not well supported by experimental data.
Phase separation can occur in refractory multicomponent HEAs.
The provided evidence contains no direct experimental data for sub-10 nm Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome place the breakdown above 700 K, but the support criterion accepts segregation and ripening anywhere below 800 K. This includes temperatures below 700 K and therefore does not cleanly test the stated threshold.
